fkszph40q7xknINSERT INTO GLBTMPACBK (TDATE, AC_NO, DRCR, CSH_TRN, PRTCLS, DEBIT, CREDIT, BALANCE, DOC_NO, ACMASTCODE, PASS, POST, CTRNNO, OTRNNO, VOU_NO, VOU_SRNO, OP_ID , SU_ID, RC_COUNT, FD_COUNT, CHQ_PREFIX, CASHIER_ID, CASHIER_OK, CASH_CR, CASH_DR, CSHR_EXCP, DENMTION , REF_ACNO, REF_ACMCD , CHQBOUNCE, FORBRANCH, ATBRANCH, VOU_GRNO , DD_GRNO, GOLD_REC_NO, DD_CLEAR, INTFRDT, INTTODT, AC_TYPE, RECEIPTNO, FD_RC_CNT , SHIFT_NO, PROC_SRNO, AC_CODE, TRNSCNID) SELECT A.TDATE, A.AC_NO, A.DRCR, A.CSH_TRN, A.PRTCLS, A.DEBIT, A.CREDIT, A.BALANCE, A.DOC_NO, A.ACMASTCODE, :"SYS_B_00", A.POST, A.CTRNNO, A.OTRNNO, A.VOU_NO, A.VOU_SRNO, A.OP_ID , A.SU_ID, A.RC_COUNT, A.FD_COUNT, A.CHQ_PREFIX, A.CASHIER_ID, A.CASHIER_OK, A.CASH_CR, A.CASH_DR, A.CSHR_EXCP, A.DENMTION , A.REF_ACNO, A.REF_ACMCD , A.CHQBOUNCE, A.FORBRANCH, A.ATBRANCH, A.VOU_GRNO , A.DD_GRNO, A.GOLD_REC_NO, A.DD_CLEAR, A.INTFRDT, A.INTTODT, A.AC_TYPE, A.RECEIPTNO, A.FD_RC_CNT , A.SHIFT_NO, A.PROC_SRNO, B.AC_CODE, A.TRNSCNID FROM ACBK A, ACMAST B WHERE A.ACMASTCODE=B.ACMASTCODE AND A.TDATE = :"SYS_B_01" AND ATBRANCH = :"SYS_B_02" AND NVL(A.CNCLED, :"SYS_B_03") !=:"SYS_B_04" AND A.TRN_TYPE = :"SYS_B_05" AND A.CSH_TRN!= :"SYS_B_06" AND NVL(A.SSD_QUICK, :"SYS_B_07")=:"SYS_B_08" AND NVL(A.SRCOFTRN, :"SYS_B_09") NOT IN (:"SYS_B_10", :"SYS_B_11", :"SYS_B_12") AND NVL(A.POST, :"SYS_B_13")<>:"SYS_B_14" ORDER BY VOU_GRNO, OTRNNO

ADDM Task ADDM:142411631_1_2851

          ADDM Report for Task 'ADDM:142411631_1_2851'
          --------------------------------------------

Analysis Period
---------------
AWR snapshot range from 2850 to 2851.
Time period starts at 19-MAY-26 11.30.50 AM
Time period ends at 19-MAY-26 12.30.14 PM

Analysis Target
---------------
Database 'NATRAJ' with DB ID 142411631.
Database version during analysis period was 19.29.0.0.0.
Database version when ADDM was executed was 19.0.0.0.0.
All recommendations generated by ADDM are valid for database version 19.0.0.0.0, the version in which ADDM was executed.
ADDM performed an analysis of instance natraj, numbered 1 and hosted at
natraj-db.

Activity During the Analysis Period
-----------------------------------
Total database time was 36782 seconds.
The average number of active sessions was 10.32.

Summary of Findings
-------------------
   Description                      Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                    Percent of Activity
   -------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------
1  Session Connect and Disconnect   1.86 | 18.04         1
2  Soft Parse                       1.56 | 15.11         2
3  Shared Pool Latches              1.27 | 12.35         1
4  Top SQL Statements               .94 | 9.15           2
5  Hard Parse Due to Invalidations  .43 | 4.19           1
6  PL/SQL Execution                 .24 | 2.37           5
7  Undersized SGA                   .2 | 1.97            1


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.86 active sessions, 18.04% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.86 active sessions, 18.04% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.56 active sessions, 15.11% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.56 active sessions, 15.11% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.56 active sessions, 15.11% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "500" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 3: Shared Pool Latches
Impact is 1.27 active sessions, 12.35% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Contention for latches related to the shared pool was consuming significant
database time.
Waits for "library cache: mutex X" amounted to 1% of database time.
Waits for "latch: shared pool" amounted to 9% of database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.27 active sessions, 12.35% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for latch contention using the given blocking
      sessions or modules.
   Rationale
      The session with ID 1518 and serial number 24736 in instance number 1
      was the blocking session responsible for 18% of this recommendation's
      benefit.
   Rationale
      The session with ID 100 and serial number 11659 in instance number 1 was
      the blocking session responsible for 15% of this recommendation's
      benefit.
   Rationale
      The session with ID 9792 and serial number 31954 in instance number 1
      was the blocking session responsible for 15% of this recommendation's
      benefit.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Concurrency" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.35 active sessions, 13.08% of total activity.


Finding 4: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .95 active sessions, 9.15% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .7 active sessions, 6.82% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 3% for SQL execution,
      30% for parsing, 67% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.

   Recommendation 2: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .21 active sessions, 2.04% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the SELECT statement with SQL_ID
      "0uwka6rtdcm0f".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 0uwka6rtdcm0f.
         SELECT COUNT(*) FROM USER_LOGOUTDET A
         WHERE   A.LOGIN_UID=:"SYS_B_0"
   Rationale
      The SQL spent 87% of its database time on CPU, I/O and Cluster waits.
      This part of database time may be improved by the SQL Tuning Advisor.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 88% for SQL
      execution, 12% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java
      execution.
